kurz: Who legally owns the securities held in a securities account, how the various providers make money, and how to recognise a suitable broker.

bloecke.md:
A securities account is a register. In Germany, the securities themselves are held by a central securities depository in a collective holding, in which each investor has fractional co-ownership. This form of custody is called [[Collective safe custody (Girosammelverwahrung)|collective safe custody (Girosammelverwahrung)]]. The broker merely keeps records of who is entitled to which portion. This looks like a formality, but it is decisive if things go wrong. If the broker goes bust, the securities are separated from the insolvency estate (Aussonderung), because they never formed part of its assets.

Every securities account comes with a [[Settlement account|settlement account]]. It holds money, such as savings plan contributions awaiting execution, dividends, sale proceeds and an uninvested buffer. Legally, this money is fundamentally different from the securities. It is a claim against the bank, in other words a loan that the customer makes to it. The bank carries the balance on its balance sheet and uses it for its business, and in insolvency it forms part of the estate. That is why deposit protection applies only to this balance.

bloecke.titel: Two legal positions from one securities account agreement
bloecke.unter: The upper path leads to a claim against the bank, the lower one to ownership; all investor protection rests on this difference.

bloecke.md: Securities in the securities account belong to the customer, regardless of the portfolio value and regardless of any protection limit. Money in the settlement account, by contrast, belongs to the bank. The customer only has a claim to it, and the protection of that claim is capped.

## Deposit protection and compensation

Statutory deposit protection covers €100,000 per customer and institution. For a joint account, each holder counts separately. After certain life events such as the sale of a property, an inheritance, a severance payment, divorce or retirement, up to €500,000 is protected for six months. Payment is to be made within seven working days.

A third level is known to only a few. If the broker is an investment firm without a banking licence and a monetary claim from a securities transaction remains outstanding, such as sale proceeds that had not yet been credited at the time of the collapse, the compensation scheme for securities trading firms (Entschädigungseinrichtung der Wertpapierhandelsunternehmen) steps in. However, it only reimburses 90% of the claim, up to a maximum of €20,000. This protection is considerably weaker than deposit protection. With a broker that has a full banking licence, such a claim counts as a deposit and is protected like a balance, at private banks through the compensation scheme of German banks (Entschädigungseinrichtung deutscher Banken). Many private banks also protect deposits voluntarily through the deposit protection fund of the Association of German Banks (Bankenverband). The limit per private customer there is being lowered step by step, from €5 million (2023) via €3 million (2025) to €1 million from 2030. Because this protection is voluntary, you should check whether your own institution is a member.

bloecke.md: The statement “But my securities account is protected up to €100,000” is wrong on two counts. The securities account does not need this protection, and the balance is only protected up to this limit. Investors who park six-figure sums in the settlement account for months after a large sale are exposed to a concentration risk where they least expect it.

## Three types of provider

High-street banks, direct banks and neobrokers differ less in how modern they are than in their revenue models. The high-street bank sells advice and finances it through initial charges, trail commissions and custody fees. The direct bank offers infrastructure, that is, many trading venues, the full range of order types and foreign stock exchanges, and charges percentage-based order fees for this. The neobroker relies on ease of use and finances itself through flat fees, subscriptions, interest margins on uninvested balances and, until the summer of 2026, inducements from the trading venue.

Neobrokers have long ceased to be a niche offering. As early as September 2025, individual providers reported around 10 million customers and customer assets of well over €100 billion. In September 2025, Scalable Capital received a full banking licence from the ECB and is therefore no longer dependent on partner banks.

bloecke.md:
## The end of payment for order flow

[[Payment for order flow]] refers to the rebate that a trading venue or market maker pays the broker for routing customer orders to it. The conflict of interest is obvious. The broker chooses the place of execution according to who pays it, instead of where the customer gets the best price. The customer sees nothing of this on the contract note, because this item is contained in the execution price.

Article 39a MiFIR has prohibited these inducements in the EU since 28 March 2024. Germany made use of the transitional option, which is why PFOF only ends for German brokers on 30 June 2026. This is the biggest restructuring of the German broker market since the rise of the neobrokers. What the trading venue used to pay now has to come from order fees, spreads, interest margins and subscription models. One large neobroker received authorisation for its own trading system in January 2026 and has executed customer orders itself since July 2026. Since the end of 2024, Scalable Capital has operated its own trading venue together with the Hanover Stock Exchange (Börse Hannover). Both steps follow the same reasoning. A broker that controls execution itself earns money from it without depending on payments from a trading venue.

bloecke.titel: Interest margin as a source of revenue
bloecke.md: In mid-September 2026, the ECB deposit facility rate stood at 2.50%. How much of this a provider passes on for uninvested balances and how much it keeps is not stated in any fee schedule. More important than the advertised interest rate is the question of who holds the money. If a bank holds it, deposit protection applies. If it is in a money market fund, it is separated from the assets of the management company as fund assets, but in return there is a small price risk.

The PFOF ban removes a conflict of interest, but it does not lower prices. Customers who have been with the same provider for years should reread the list of prices and services in 2026 and not rely on the terms of 2023.

## Costs of a securities account

A cost comparison that only looks at the order fee says little. The costs arise in at least seven places, and the largest items rarely appear in the published price list.

bloecke.md: In the end, a percentage fee costs exactly its percentage of the final wealth. An execution fee of 1.75% therefore means 1.75% less portfolio value, regardless of how long you save. A fixed amount, by contrast, becomes relatively cheaper the higher the monthly contribution. With a contribution of €200, €1.50 corresponds to 0.75%, and with €600 to only 0.25%.

## Securities account transfer

Switching provider does not require selling. According to the case law of the Federal Court of Justice (BGH), German banks may not charge a fee of their own for a securities account transfer. They may only pass on the third-party costs they incurred in the process. For a transfer within Germany without a change of owner, the tax acquisition data are transferred along with the securities. Purchase price, purchase date and holding period are preserved, and no taxable event arises.

There are two sources of error here. The first concerns transfers to another person, such as a partner or a child. In that case, the customer must expressly notify the bank that the transfer is made without payment. Without this notification, the bank treats the transaction as a sale and immediately deducts capital income withholding tax (Kapitalertragsteuer). The second source of error is missing acquisition data, which is the norm for transfers from a foreign broker. In this case, the German bank applies a [[Substitute tax base (Ersatzbemessungsgrundlage)|substitute tax base (Ersatzbemessungsgrundlage)]] of 30% of the sale proceeds.

A position is sold for €10,000, and the actual gain is €500. With complete data, the tax on this comes to around €132 (26.375%, without church tax). Without data, the bank applies 30% of €10,000, that is, a tax base of €3,000, and withholds around €791. That is six times as much. The excess amount withheld can only be recovered through the tax return. For this you need documents from the old securities account, which you should therefore keep.

## Foreign brokers

A foreign broker based in the EU is legally unproblematic. The securities remain the customer's property, the assets of UCITS funds remain separate from the assets of the management company, and there is a compensation scheme. However, it is that of the country where the broker is based, with its own limits and, in the event of a dispute, its own language. The practical difference lies in tax. German brokers automatically pay over the capital income withholding tax of 25% plus the solidarity surcharge and, where applicable, church tax, manage the [[Exemption order (Freistellungsauftrag)|exemption order (Freistellungsauftrag)]] and keep the loss offset pots. With a foreign broker, none of this happens. You have to declare sales, dividends and currency conversions yourself in the capital income annex (Anlage KAP), and the burden of proof lies with the investor.

This does not rule out a foreign broker, but it is a question of time and effort. An investor who pays into two world ETFs through savings plans gains almost nothing from a foreign broker and has additional work with the tax return every year. For investors who write options or trade on exchanges that German providers do not connect to, on the other hand, there is a genuine reason.

The saver's allowance (Sparer-Pauschbetrag) is €1,000 per person per year, or €2,000 for joint assessment. The bank only takes it into account when withholding tax if an exemption order has been submitted, and the exemption orders at several banks may not exceed the allowance in total. Without an exemption order, the allowance can be claimed in the tax return using the capital income annex. In addition, losses from share sales may only be offset against gains from share sales, and therefore not against ETF gains, interest or dividends.

schritte.text: Look up the provider in the company database of BaFin (Federal Financial Supervisory Authority) or check whether it operates as a notified EU institution. Do not invest any money without an entry.

Find out whether the settlement account is held at a bank with statutory deposit protection or whether interest is paid via partner banks or a money market fund. This information is in the small print and not in the advertising.

schritte.titel: Read the price list instead of the home page
schritte.text: Go through all seven cost items, including the foreign currency surcharge and the trading venue fee. In 2026 this is particularly important, because pricing models were rebuilt after the end of PFOF.

schritte.titel: Check trading venues and order types
schritte.text: Check whether the trading venue offered is sufficient for the purchases you want to make and whether limit orders and, if needed, stop variants are available. A provider without limit orders is unsuitable for lump-sum investments.
Check whether the ETF you want is available as a savings plan, how many execution dates there are and whether the fee exemption applies permanently or is part of a time-limited promotional list.

A securities account transfer must be possible free of charge, and the acquisition data must be transferred as well. Otherwise, switching later is difficult, and the customer remains tied to the provider.

bloecke.md: Almost every provider advertises a securities-backed or Lombard loan, because it earns an interest margin on the existing portfolio without tying up new capital. The loan is secured on the portfolio value at a lending ratio that varies widely depending on asset class and institution. The problem is that several things happen at the same time. If the market falls, the portfolio value and the lending value fall together. The bank then makes a margin call, at exactly the moment when putting up more money is hardest. If the customer does not respond, the bank may realise the collateral. In this way, a temporary fall in prices becomes a permanent loss that goes back to a decision made months earlier.

mitnehmen: Securities in the securities account are the customer's property and do not become part of the broker's insolvency estate; only the balance in the settlement account needs deposit protection.

Protection is tiered: €100,000 as a rule, up to €500,000 for six months after certain life events, and only 90% up to a maximum of €20,000 for outstanding monetary claims from securities transactions with an investment firm.
Payment for order flow ends for German brokers on 30 June 2026; the conflict of interest disappears, revenue shifts to fees, spreads and interest margins, and price lists should be reread in 2026.
A percentage savings plan fee ultimately costs exactly its percentage of the final wealth, while a fixed amount becomes relatively cheaper as the monthly contribution rises.
In a securities account transfer, the tax burden depends on whether the acquisition data are transferred as well; if they are missing, 30% of the sale proceeds is used as the tax base.

begriffe.text: The cash account that comes with every securities account. The balance in it is a claim against the bank and is covered by deposit protection, unlike the securities in the securities account.

Standard form of securities custody in Germany. All units of a class are held by a central securities depository in a collective holding, in which the investor has fractional co-ownership. This is why they can be separated from the estate if the broker becomes insolvent.

Rebate paid by a trading venue or market maker to the broker for customer orders routed to it. Banned in the EU since 28 March 2024 (Article 39a MiFIR), in Germany with a transition period until 30 June 2026.

If the bank lacks the acquisition data for a security, under Section 43a(2) sentence 7 EStG (Income Tax Act) it applies a flat 30% of the sale proceeds as the taxable amount. This can only be corrected through the tax return.
